neighbours.label: Fires on nouns and modifiers that name components of a software system (graphics engines, drivers, libraries, modules, custom-built components) in descriptions of software; quiet on the same words describing hardware, print art or crafts.
fire: Unity ships with a physics engine and a graphics pipeline for mobile games.
The vendor bundles proprietary software libraries with every industrial controller.
Python offers a huge ecosystem of community-maintained packages on PyPI.
The toolkit exposes a plugin interface so developers can write custom modules.
OpenGL provides a cross-platform graphics API used by many game studios.
Their compiler includes an optimizer and a code generator written in Rust.
The framework lets teams register custom-defined components in the user interface.
MATLAB supplies built-in solvers and toolboxes for signal processing software.
quiet: The workshop sells a hydraulic press and a paint booth for car bodies.
The vendor bundles proprietary steel brackets with every industrial shelf.
The market offers a huge selection of community-grown vegetables on Sundays.
The quilt pattern lets beginners stitch custom borders around each square.
The gallery shows hand-drawn graphics from an old travel poster series.
Their bakery includes a bread oven and a dough mixer bought in Italy.
The tailor lets customers choose custom-made buttons for their jackets.
The hardware store supplies built-in shelves and cabinets for kitchens.

predictions: 6/8 fire >= 0.2 (probes: 'graphics rendering engine' 0.75, 'custom-developed software drivers' 0.46, 'user-supplied modules through CRAN' 0.20); near misses <= 0.1 ('graphics card' 0.06, bakery 'custom-developed' 0.05).
